appraisal_events.evidence: « c'est le moment où un homme sain d'esprit qui cause avec un fou ne s'est pas encore aperçu que c'est un fou » ; « j'eus peine à me retenir de ne pas embrasser ses douces mains blanches et fripées » ; plus tard Norpois raconte qu'il avait « vu le moment où j'allais lui baiser les mains » et « je ne rougis pas seulement jusqu'aux oreilles ».
appraisal_events.explanation: The retrospective narrator stages his younger self as a monomaniac whose gushing near-kiss of Norpois's unappetizing hands was noticed, remembered, and later retailed as gossip, so the dominant local movement is a self-endorsed diminishment of the narrator through exposure and shame.

appraisal_events.evidence: « je ne crois pas qu'elle approchera jamais de sa mère, si je peux dire cela sans blesser en vous un sentiment trop vif »
appraisal_events.explanation: In the opening dialogue Norpois grants Gilberte only mild charm and ranks her permanently below her mother, a comparative appraisal that lowers Gilberte while raising Odette; the narrator's dissent registers but does not cancel the diplomat's verdict.

status_effects.explanation: He is locally reduced to a figure of comic obsession, likened to a madman and caught in an absurd gesture that becomes an anecdote at his expense.
His effusive dependence on Norpois's mediation, and the later blush of stupefaction on learning he was talked about, leave him emotionally exposed and without leverage.
Norpois's authoritative comparison places her below her mother as merely 'charmante', a mild local downgrade.
She is elevated as the standard of beauty her daughter will never reach, and is separately the object of the narrator's avowed admiration.

ambiguities: The closing revelation of the 'potin' could be read as diminishing Norpois instead, since the man praised as 'habitué par sa profession et ses origines à la discrétion' turns out to retail the scene; the reading taken here keeps the narrator as target because the shame, the blush, and the epistemological lesson are all his, while Norpois's indiscretion is reported without reproach.

Norpois's 'grand prestige' and importance are given in free indirect style from the young narrator's inflated viewpoint (the Olympian-divinity simile, the wrinkled water-logged hands), so the passage neither clearly endorses nor clearly denies any gain in Norpois's own standing; no status effect is recorded for him.
